seo.title: LanBeam — LAN file transfer & real-time sharing
seo.description: LanBeam is a local-first LAN file transfer and real-time sharing tool. No accounts, no cloud service — any device on the same network uploads, downloads, and shares text and images right from the browser.

hero.titleB: every device on the LAN shares in seconds
hero.desc: LanBeam is a local-first file transfer and real-time sharing tool for your network. Launch it on one machine and any device on the same network can upload, download, and share text and images right from the browser — no accounts, and nothing ever touches the cloud.
hero.platformNote: macOS / Windows / Linux · Standalone binary · Install via npm / winget / curl
hero.terminalAria: Terminal example: install and launch LanBeam

terminal.tip: 💡 Other devices can access the file transfer service via the LAN address above

features.title: What it does
features.desc: A lightweight service running on your computer that covers the most common sharing needs on your LAN.

items.title: Drag-and-drop transfer
items.desc: Drag files or whole folders into the browser to upload, keeping the directory structure intact. Every device can download or delete at any time.

items.title: Real-time sharing
items.desc: One shared note, synced in real time across every open device. Paste an image and it's instantly visible — perfect for swapping screenshots.

items.title: Zero-friction access
items.desc: The other side needs nothing installed — just send the address; any browser opens it instantly, on phones and computers alike.

items.title: Local-first
items.desc: Files live only on the machine running LanBeam. No accounts, no cloud drives — traffic never leaves your LAN.

items.title: Large files, no sweat
items.desc: Supports files up to 200MB by default, adjustable with --max-size. LAN transfers run at full bandwidth.

items.title: Private & secure
items.desc: Shared notes and images live in memory only and are wiped the moment the server stops. Nothing is uploaded, and there is no telemetry.

steps.title: Get started in 3 steps
steps.desc: From installation to your first connected device in under a minute.

items.title: Install
items.desc: macOS and Linux get a standalone binary via a one-line script — no Node.js needed; Windows uses winget or a direct download.

items.title: Launch
items.desc: Run lanbeam in your terminal. The service starts on port 3001 and automatically increments to find a free port when it's taken.

items.title: Connect
items.desc: Send the LAN address from your terminal to any device on the same network. Opening it in a browser enables upload, download, and sharing — nothing to install on the other side.

install.title: Install it your way
install.desc: LanBeam ships as an npm package, with standalone executables for macOS, Linux, and Windows plus a winget channel. Pick whichever you prefer.

channels.title: Run from source
channels.cmd: git clone && pnpm install && pnpm dev

terminal.commentIncrement: # auto-increment when the port is taken (3001 → 3020)

privacy.title: Your data stays entirely on your LAN
privacy.desc1: LanBeam has no server side and collects no data. Uploaded files live only on the machine running it; shared text and images exist in memory only and are cleared the moment the process stops.
privacy.desc2: Only devices on the same network can reach it — nothing outside your LAN can, there are no accounts, and there's no cloud relay.

points.title: No accounts, no cloud
points.desc: no service in the middle logging your activity

points.title: Files stay on your machine
points.desc: uploads go to the lanbeam-files/ directory and are gone when deleted

points.title: Text & images in memory only
points.desc: cleared when the server stops — never written to disk, never persisted

points.title: LAN-only boundary
points.desc: bound to LAN addresses only; unreachable from outside networks

items.q: Do recipients need LanBeam installed to receive files?
items.a: No. Just send them the LAN address from your terminal — anyone can open it in any browser (phone, tablet, or computer) to upload and download. With LanBeam, the browser is the client.

items.q: Does it work over the internet (not on the same Wi-Fi)?
items.a: No — LanBeam is designed to be a LAN tool. Devices must be on the same network (same Wi-Fi or wired). This guarantees your data never leaves the LAN and never touches the cloud.

items.q: Is there a per-file size limit?
items.a: By default each file is capped at 200MB. Use lanbeam --max-size 500 to allow 500MB, or set the MAX_FILE_SIZE environment variable.

items.q: What if the port is already in use?
items.a: It starts on port 3001 by default; if taken, it automatically increments (3001 → 3020) until a free port is found and prints the actual address. You can also set one manually with lanbeam --port 8080.
In the lanbeam-files/ directory under where you run LanBeam (server/uploads/ when running from source). Files are written as ordinary files, so you can access, back up, or delete them anytime.

items.q: Are shared text and images saved?
items.a: No. They only live in server memory (up to the last 20 images, 10MB each); everything is cleared when the server stops and is never written to disk.

items.q: Do I need to register or pay?
items.a: Not at all. LanBeam is free, open source (MIT), and has no account system. Install and go — your files and data stay on your own devices.

cta.desc: Install once, launch anytime. No accounts, no cloud uploads, no third parties — the fastest way to move files on your LAN.
